title: A chg snapshot is addressed by its content and can be built in the job's own tree

story.as_a: CI job or holder that needs a warm build
story.i_want_to: name a chg snapshot by what it was built from (tree, toolchain, build path) and build it in the tree I am working in
story.so_that: any machine can tell whether a snapshot fits its tree before it uses one, and a snapshot built on one machine can serve another

rationale: PRD R8: warm state is a read-only, content-addressed snapshot that chg builds and any machine can fetch or rebuild. Today a snapshot is named by commit sha only (chg/cli/src/store.rs:36-50), lives in a per-machine, per-clone store (store.rs:147-158), and is built only at that store's build path under one build lock (snapshot.rs:99-121), so twelve CI slots on one host would queue on it and no other machine can use it. Its toolchain is not recorded at all, which is how a PLT holding another slot's OTP paths killed dialyzer on 2026-08-03 (KB 09245ceb). This story gives a snapshot a content key and an in-place build; publishing and fetching it is US-52.57.

acceptance_criteria.description: `chg snapshot key <repo> <sha>` prints one JSON line {"key", "sha", "tree", "build_path", "toolchain"}; key is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the newline-joined fields: `chg-snapshot-v1`, the commit's tree id, the resolved build path, the adapter's toolchain string, the adapter kind and contract version, and the target OS and arch.
Two commits with the same tree id, built at the same path with the same toolchain, get the same key; changing any one of tree, path or toolchain changes the key.

The adapter contract gains an optional `toolchain` command; the Elixir adapter's `mix chg.toolchain` prints {"toolchain": "elixir=V;otp=O;root=R"}, where V is System.version(), O is the full OTP version from the OTP_VERSION file and R is :code.root_dir(). An adapter without the command gives the toolchain `none`.

`chg snapshot build --here <sha>` builds the snapshot in the current work tree, which must be at <sha>, by running the adapter's `snapshot` command there, then copies (clones where the filesystem allows) the tree into the local store as `snapshots/<sha>` with meta fields `key`, `toolchain` and `built_in` = the tree's resolved path; it takes no build lock, because the tree is the caller's own.

`chg snapshot build --here` refuses a tree with modified or untracked files (git status --porcelain not empty, ignored files excepted): exit 2, naming the first ten paths, and nothing is written to the store.
A second `chg snapshot build --here` for a key the local store already holds prints {"status":"exists","key":...} and runs no adapter command.

`chg ws hydrate` never hydrates from a snapshot whose recorded toolchain differs from the adapter's current toolchain: such a snapshot is skipped as if absent (exit 3 when no other fits), and stderr names both toolchains. A snapshot with no recorded toolchain (built before this story) is still used, as today.

test_cases.name: key derivation over tree, path and toolchain (cargo unit test in chg/cli)
preconditions: a temp git repo with commits A and B whose trees are equal, and C with a changed file
a stub adapter whose toolchain command prints a fixed string
steps: snapshot::key for A and B at one path
key for C; key for A at another path; key for A with the stub toolchain changed
expected_results: A == B; the other three each differ from A and from each other

test_cases.name: mix chg.toolchain prints the running toolchain (ExUnit in chg/adapters/elixir)
steps: run Mix.Tasks.Chg.Toolchain and decode its JSON

test_cases.name: an in-place build lands in the store under its key, and a second is a no-op (chg integration test, Elixir fixture)
preconditions: adapters/elixir/fixtures/sample checked out clean in a temp dir; CHG_STORE a temp dir
steps: chg snapshot build --here HEAD again with an adapter wrapper that records its invocations
expected_results: meta carries key, toolchain and built_in = the tree's path; the second run prints status exists and invokes nothing

test_cases.name: a dirty tree is refused
preconditions: a clean fixture tree with one tracked file edited and one untracked file added
expected_results: exit 2; stderr names both paths; snapshots/ is empty

test_cases.name: hydrate skips a snapshot built with another toolchain, uses one with none recorded
preconditions: a store holding a snapshot of HEAD whose meta toolchain is elixir=0.0.0;otp=0;root=/x
steps: chg ws hydrate in a fresh worktree
rewrite the meta without a toolchain field; hydrate again in another fresh worktree
expected_results: first exits 3 and names both toolchains; second hydrates

technical_notes: Today's paths are in /home/mkreyman/workspace/chg; release 2 moves them under chg/ in this repo (README names table: chg source in this repo). Cite and edit the moved files.

Meta: cli/src/store.rs:36-50 (sha, built_at_ms, from, work, ms, built_in); add `key` and `toolchain` as #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none)] like built_in (:48), so old meta files still parse. Meta::is_built_at at :55.

Store layout and root: store.rs:1-17, root() at :64, Store::for_repo at :147 (store dir keyed by the clone's common dir), build_dir at :222, list at :257, nearest_ancestor at :273, gc at :322 (KEEP = 3 at :30). The in-place build writes into the same snapshots/<sha> dir, so list, nearest_ancestor, lease and GC need no change.

The existing build: snapshot.rs:60 build/3 and :80 build_inner/4 (build lock at :99-109, build dir clear at :120-122, adapter invoke at :160-170, meta at :172-182, swap into place under the exclusive lock at :195-211). --here reuses the meta write and the swap; it skips the lock, the clone-from-base and apply_diff (:224).
Tree id: `git rev-parse <sha>^{tree}` through git::cmd as snapshot.rs:225 does. SHA-256 comes from the sha2 crate chg already uses for HMAC (outbox.rs:174).

Adapter contract: CommandName and its placeholders at cli/src/contract.rs:90-94, manifest fields at :119 and :158; add `toolchain` as an optional command with no placeholders. Elixir adapter manifest adapters/elixir/adapter.toml; the snapshot task is lib/mix/tasks/chg.snapshot.ex (its own idempotence key at :99-110 already joins System.version and otp_release; the new task reads the full OTP version from Path.join([:code.root_dir(), "releases", otp_release, "OTP_VERSION"])).

Hydrate: cli/src/ws.rs:52 hydrate/1 picks the nearest ancestor at :68; filter by toolchain before that pick. CLI wiring: cli/src/main.rs:426 SnapshotCmd (add Key and the --here flag on Build), dispatch at :517-532.

Why the toolchain is in the key and the hydrate filter: a PLT records 552 paths under the Erlang install and 383 under Elixir (KB 09245ceb), so a snapshot from another OTP root is wrong, not merely slow.
non_goals: Uploading and downloading snapshots between machines: US-52.57.
Running CI jobs in per-job trees that use these snapshots: US-52.58.
Changing the shadow check or gate-mode `chg check`, which keep building at the store's build path under the build lock.

failure_modes.partition: n/a: a local CLI over the local git repo and the local store; no network call in this story.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.56.4: the snapshot lives in the machine's store as a cache; losing it costs a rebuild, and its meta records the key, toolchain and path that decide whether it fits a tree.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.56.6: a repeated build of a key the store holds does nothing, so a retried job never builds twice.
failure_modes.slow: n/a: no network; the adapter's snapshot command keeps its existing wall-clock cap (cli/src/exec.rs:34 cap).
failure_modes.reach: n/a: runs inline in the chg process the caller started, in the caller's own tree.

definition_of_done: On minis, `chg snapshot key ~/workspace/loopctl HEAD` twice prints the same key, and the key changes after `asdf` switches Erlang to another installed version.
`chg snapshot build --here HEAD` in a clean loopctl checkout leaves snapshots/<sha>/.chg-snapshot.json carrying key and toolchain.
defaults: Key version string `chg-snapshot-v1`; bumping it invalidates every published snapshot (owner may change).
Dirty-tree refusal lists at most ten paths.
